nodes.label: Bayesian Optimisation / Active Learning
nodes.rationale: BO is for choosing the next experiment, not for mining a fixed surrogate. With no synthesis loop its core value proposition is absent and NSGA-II is strictly simpler; if a collaborator will actually synthesise alloys, this judgement inverts.

nodes.label: Cost, Criticality and Toxicity Screen
nodes.rationale: Cost is a deterministic function of composition, so it costs nothing to add as an objective and immediately makes the Pareto front more interesting; the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index flags supply-concentration risk, and Be/Cd toxicity is flagged outright.

nodes.label: Enumerate-and-Screen (Architecture A)
nodes.rationale: Recommended first build (5-8 developer-days) because it reuses the existing CBFV pipeline and CatBoost model with no new model, no inversion and no new maths; failure modes stay printable and debuggable, and it degrades gracefully into NSGA-II when the enumeration blows up. Main risk is combinatorial explosion; mitigation is one alloy family per run and a coarse 0.05 fraction grid.

nodes.label: Constrained Multi-Objective EA (Architecture B)
nodes.rationale: Proposed thesis centrepiece: NSGA-II/III over the composition simplex with the surrogate as objective and physics rules as constraints, producing a Pareto front instead of a single best alloy. Because the objectives are cheap surrogate calls, an evolutionary algorithm beats Bayesian optimisation in this regime.

nodes.label: pymoo
nodes.rationale: Purpose-built MOO framework with better diagnostics, hypervolume tooling and MCDM than Optuna; recommended for the thesis-grade run where the EA itself is the contribution.

nodes.label: Streamlit Screening App
nodes.rationale: Pure-Python and the fastest path from script to interactive app, good with dataframes and Plotly which is already a dependency; Dash is the choice only if the app must outlive the thesis, and FastAPI + React is explicitly wrong for a one-person project.

nodes.label: Inverse Design Methods Memo
nodes.rationale: Research memo, no code written; every factual claim is linked to a primary source and unverifiable claims are explicitly marked unverified. Package versions read from the PyPI and GitHub REST APIs on 2026-08-29.

nodes.label: HYST Baseline Performance Gap
nodes.rationale: HyStor's own HYST model reached MAE 0.29 / R2 0.79 on the same 1282-point database while this project reports test R2 0.951 on a formula-disjoint stratified split. The gap is plausibly genuine (different split protocol, target transform and a tuned CatBoost) but the thesis must address it head-on; a leave-one-alloy-class-out number is the cleanest way to settle it.

nodes.label: research/ Folder Convention
nodes.rationale: Root-level prose (README.md, REPORT.md) documents the forward model that exists; forward-looking literature reviews and design memos describe work that does not exist yet, so they get their own directory rather than polluting either.

nodes.label: CatBoost Native Uncertainty
nodes.rationale: Quantile, MultiQuantile and RMSEWithUncertainty plus virtual ensembles (several predictions from one trained model by truncation) - lowest-friction option because CatBoost is already a project dependency and needs zero new packages.

nodes.label: Conformal Prediction Intervals
nodes.rationale: Distribution-free finite-sample coverage on top of any point model, including the existing stacking ensemble; also the standard way to operationalise an applicability domain in cheminformatics.

nodes.label: Lower-Confidence-Bound Ranking
nodes.rationale: Rank candidates by the 10th-percentile prediction rather than the mean; this penalises candidates the model is unsure about automatically, with no extra machinery.

nodes.label: Uncertainty Quantification Guard Rail
nodes.rationale: A global optimizer maximising a tree ensemble will find and exploit regions where the model is confidently wrong, because tree ensembles extrapolate as constants and the search is explicitly hunting extremes. Ranking by predicted mean alone is the single most likely way this project produces nonsense.

nodes.label: Applicability Domain and Novelty Control
nodes.rationale: Because models generalise within an alloy family but not across families, a candidate from an unfamiliar corner of composition space is not merely uncertain, it is out of scope. Three screens: ElMD distance to the training set, Alloy_class assignability, and extrapolative validation before trusting any of it.

nodes.label: Conditional Generative Design (Architecture C)
nodes.rationale: Stretch goal with a real chance of a null result (30-45 developer-days). Framed so that failure is publishable: quantifying the data threshold below which generative inverse design does not pay off for hydrides is itself a contribution.

nodes.label: Element Mover's Distance (ElMD)
nodes.rationale: Chemically intuitive composition-to-composition distance on a modified Pettifor scale; reporting ElMD to the nearest known alloy turns 'novel' from an assertion into a number. Note GPL-3.0, which matters if the app is distributed.

nodes.label: Leave-One-Cluster/Class-Out Validation
nodes.rationale: A formula-disjoint stratified split still measures interpolation across chemical space, not extrapolation into new families; the class-held-out R2 is expected to be substantially lower than 0.951, and saying so is itself a contribution.

nodes.label: Do-Not-Rediscover-Known-Alloys Check
nodes.rationale: Any 'unreported composition' claim is only meaningful if the candidate was checked against the merged HyStor + ML-HydPARK table, the HyMARC database and the general databases via OPTIMADE, with the ElMD distance to the nearest known alloy reported.

nodes.label: OPTIMADE Federated Query API
nodes.rationale: One query across AFLOW, COD, Materials Cloud, Materials Project, NOMAD, odbx and OQMD - preferred over maintaining four separate stale clients.

nodes.label: Generative-Model Data Scale Argument
nodes.rationale: Three independent reasons not to start with a VAE/GAN/diffusion model at 1280 rows: published materials generative models work at 1e4-1e6 examples (MatterGen ~600k, CDVAE MP-20 45,231, MatGAN on ICSD); Matbench and MODNet show descriptor-based classical ML stays competitive below ~1e4 samples, so a generative model is hopeless where a discriminative deep model is already marginal; and the effective chemical diversity is below 1280 because the split works on unique formulae.

nodes.label: Miedema Formation-Enthalpy Model
nodes.rationale: Miedema's reverse-stability rule - a lower host-compound formation enthalpy gives a more stable hydride - is a useful sanity direction, and the project already computes Mixing enthalpy and Miedema_deltaH_ss_min so the machinery exists.
nodes.community_name: Raw Data Diagnostics and Physics Screens

nodes.label: Physical Validity Filters
nodes.rationale: Layered cheapest-first: simplex constraint with a minimum non-zero fraction, family stoichiometry (AB5/AB2/AB/A2B), VEC windows, Hume-Rothery / HEA solid-solution criteria, then Miedema enthalpies. Family stoichiometry is the highest-value single filter because it collapses the space and guarantees candidates look like real hydride chemistry.
nodes.community_name: Raw Data Diagnostics and Physics Screens

nodes.label: van 't Hoff Thermodynamic Screen
nodes.rationale: ln p_H2 = dH/RT - dS/R, and dS is roughly constant at ~130 J/K/mol across metal-hydrogen systems, so a single predicted dH nearly suffices to place a candidate on a temperature/pressure map - high value for low cost if a dH model is trained from ML-HydPARK.
nodes.community_name: Raw Data Diagnostics and Physics Screens

nodes.label: Valence Electron Concentration Windows
nodes.rationale: AB2 hydrogen storage alloys: VEC 6.2-6.5 with size mismatch delta >= 9.7%; BCC alloys destabilise hydride above VEC ~4.75 with the best capacity/cyclability compromise in 4.75-5.0. These windows are family-specific and must not be applied globally.
nodes.community_name: Raw Data Diagnostics and Physics Screens

nodes.label: Optuna NSGA-II/III Samplers
nodes.rationale: Recommended for the MVP because Optuna is already a project dependency and both samplers accept constraints_func with constrained-domination handling - a multi-objective constrained search needs zero new packages.

nodes.label: Feature-Space Inversion (Option B)
nodes.rationale: Rejected: optimising the 22 descriptors freely then decoding by nearest-match still needs an enumerated library, and in between it lets the optimizer wander into descriptor vectors no composition can produce. Worth building only as a contrast experiment demonstrating why Option A is correct.

nodes.label: Optimise in Composition Space (Option A)
nodes.rationale: Parameterise a candidate as (element subset, simplex fractions, temperature), build the formula string, re-run CBFV generate_features and subset to the 22 descriptors - every candidate is a real composition by construction. Requires reusing the exact fitted RobustScaler (refitting on candidates is a silent correctness bug) and batched featurisation for throughput.

nodes.label: Descriptor Non-Invertibility
nodes.rationale: composition to descriptor is well-defined but many-to-one, so descriptor to composition is ill-posed. The resolution is to never invert it: optimise in composition space and evaluate the map forwards only.

nodes.label: Capacity Prediction from Formula and Temperature
nodes.rationale: Inputs are deliberately restricted to chemical formula plus operating temperature because those are known before synthesis; measuring capacity experimentally is slow and expensive, so a composition-only surrogate can screen candidates first.
nodes.norm_label: capacity prediction from formula and temperature

nodes.label: Future Directions
nodes.rationale: Add pressure/PCT inputs, try structure-aware GNNs (MEGNet, CGCNN), combine with genetic algorithms or Bayesian optimisation for inverse alloy design, and extend to HEAs via transfer learning.

nodes.label: Stacking Ensemble (best overall)
nodes.rationale: StackingRegressor over ExtraTrees + CatBoost + GradientBoosting + RandomForest with a Ridge meta-learner; chosen as headline model for Val R2 0.939 / Test R2 0.892.

nodes.label: 13-Model Regression Benchmark
nodes.rationale: 5-fold StratifiedKFold CV with a RobustScaler inside a scikit-learn Pipeline; metrics reported in log and original wt% scale. Linear models (Lasso, ElasticNet) collapse to R2 ~ 0, which is the evidence that the structure-property relation is strongly nonlinear.

nodes.label: Bootstrap Confidence Intervals (2000 resamples)
nodes.rationale: Used to show that a point-estimate R2 ranking is not enough: ExtraTrees has the narrowest CI (0.053) and therefore the highest stability, while overlapping intervals show CatBoost is statistically indistinguishable.

nodes.label: Baseline Stacking Ensemble
nodes.rationale: Recommended production model despite ExtraTrees winning on test R2: it has the lowest overfitting (0.039), a statistically significant absolute-error reduction vs ExtraTrees (t = -2.102, p = 0.037) and is more robust across temperature subgroups.

nodes.label: ANOVA, Tukey HSD and Paired t-Tests
nodes.rationale: Model-group ANOVA (F = 11.524, p = 8.7e-8) plus FDR-BH corrected pairwise tests establish which performance gaps are real; boosting beats linear but not tree, and CatBoost is not significantly different from ExtraTrees.
nodes.norm_label: anova, tukey hsd and paired t-tests

nodes.label: Weighted Selection Score
nodes.rationale: 0.6 x R2_orig + 0.4 / MAE_orig - blends variance explained with absolute error in real wt% units so the top-4 picked for stacking are not chosen on R2 alone.

nodes.label: Optimised Stacking Overfitting Regression
nodes.rationale: Stacking built on Optuna-tuned base models got worse, not better (Test R2 0.717 vs 0.892, overfitting 0.144 vs 0.039) - the meta-learner overfit already-tuned base predictions, so the baseline ensemble stayed the recommended model.

nodes.label: CBFV Featurisation (Magpie + JARVIS)
nodes.rationale: Physics-informed compositional descriptors are used instead of structure-based ones because only the chemical formula is available at screening time.

nodes.label: Stratified Dataset Splits (896/136/247)
nodes.rationale: StratifiedShuffleSplit over 5 quantile bins of the target so that train, validation and test carry matched target distributions (log means 1.022 / 1.017 / 1.023).

nodes.label: Unique-Formulae Split Basis (1149 of 1279)
nodes.rationale: Splitting on the 1149 unique formulae rather than the 1279 rows prevents the same chemistry measured at several temperatures from straddling train and test, which would leak the answer. It still measures interpolation across chemical space, not extrapolation into unseen alloy families.

nodes.label: Model Limitations
nodes.rationale: Sparse data above 500 K, SHAP independence assumption, missing equilibrium pressure (no PCT curves), limited HEA coverage so >5-element alloys are effectively out of distribution, and log-scale SHAP directions.

nodes.label: Temperature Subgroup Performance
nodes.rationale: Splitting the test set into low (<300 K), mid (300-500 K) and high (>500 K) exposes that accuracy tracks data density: R2 0.951 in the data-rich mid band collapses to 0.824 above 500 K where only 39 samples exist.

nodes.label: SHAP Interpretation Limitations
nodes.rationale: Three caveats recorded alongside the SHAP output: values assume feature independence and residual post-VIF multicollinearity distorts attributions; explanations are relative to whichever training distribution is used as background; and with a log-scaled target the interpretation holds only in transformed space, not original units.
nodes.community_name: Raw Data Diagnostics and Physics Screens

nodes.label: log1p Target Transformation
nodes.rationale: Applied because the raw H2 wt% distribution is right-skewed (Shapiro-Wilk W = 0.8684, p = 0.000); log1p cut skewness 72% (1.57 to 0.44) and kurtosis 85% (3.01 to 0.44), stabilising variance and improving accuracy. Cost: SHAP attributions then live in log space, not wt%.
nodes.community_name: Raw Data Diagnostics and Physics Screens

nodes.label: Optuna-Optimised CatBoost
nodes.rationale: Highest validation R2 of any experiment (0.969) with negative overfitting (-0.018); preferred when a single interpretable model is required rather than an ensemble.

nodes.label: Optuna Hyperparameter Optimisation
nodes.rationale: 100 trials, TPE sampler with median pruner, applied to five top models. Only CatBoost, XGBoost and GradientBoosting improved significantly; ExtraTrees and RandomForest were already well-tuned at their defaults.

nodes.label: Machine_Model Dependency Stack
nodes.rationale: Pinned by role rather than version; matminer, pymatgen and rdkit are flagged in both READMEs as conda-forge installs because their compiled dependencies do not resolve cleanly through pip.

nodes.label: Mutual Information vs Pearson Analysis
nodes.rationale: The MI minus |Pearson| gap is used as a nonlinearity detector: dev_specific_heat (0.457), avg_polzbl_divi_atom_mass (0.375) and range_Mendeleev_Number (0.345) carry signal that linear correlation misses entirely.

nodes.label: avg_is_alkaline
nodes.rationale: Strongest linear predictor (r = +0.673): alkaline and alkaline-earth elements (Mg, Ca, La) form strong ionic/covalent hydrides with high gravimetric capacity; Mg drives the highest per-element mean capacity (3.32 wt%).

nodes.label: avg_polzbl_divi_atom_mass
nodes.rationale: Polarizability per atomic mass; Boruta/SHAP rank 1 (0.172) and MI = 0.849. Controls how electron clouds distort under an H field, linking to interstitial site geometry; the positive effect saturates near 0.5, consistent with lattice-strain limits in AB2/AB5 alloys.

nodes.label: avg_valence_d
nodes.rationale: SHAP rank 1 (0.179) and r = -0.713: higher d-electron counts in transition metals compete for bonding orbitals and reduce hydrogen affinity; capacity drops sharply beyond avg_valence_d > 2.5 per PDP analysis.

nodes.label: dev_Zunger_radii_sum
nodes.rationale: Atomic size deviation (r = -0.404, MI = 0.630): large size mismatch raises lattice strain and cuts the number of viable H-insertion sites, explaining why complex multi-component alloys sometimes underperform simple binaries/ternaries.

nodes.label: SHAP TreeExplainer Interpretability
nodes.rationale: SHAP values are computed on the log-transformed target and assume feature independence; residual post-VIF multicollinearity may distort magnitudes, so attributions are treated as an approximate guide.

nodes.label: temperature(K)
nodes.rationale: The only experimental (non-compositional) input; r = +0.500 reflects thermodynamic activation, but its low SHAP weight shows alloy chemistry dominates operating temperature for capacity prediction.

nodes.label: Five-Stage Feature Selection Pipeline
nodes.rationale: VarianceThreshold > 0.01, correlation filter |r| > 0.1, RandomForest importance > 0.005, BorutaPy all-relevant selection, then SHAP + VIF < 30 - each stage removes a different failure mode (constants, irrelevance, weak signal, redundancy, multicollinearity) so no single criterion has to do all the work.

nodes.label: CleanLab Label-Quality Screening
nodes.rationale: CleanLearning wraps a HistGradientBoostingRegressor (max_iter=300, early stopping) and flags anomalous labels from cross-validated residuals, removing literature transcription noise before model selection.
